contexts.text: Which... surpass every idea of human imagination. AC 3220:end. HH 412.
Imaginative things present themselves as not unlike visual ones.

To the exterior or corporeal memory belongs all the imaginative, which is the interior Sensuous with man, and which is vigorous especially with children and in the first age of adolescence. NJHD 48:5.

The imagination of man is nothing except the forms and shapes of such things as he has taken up with the sight of the body, wonderfully varied, and, so to speak, modified. But his interior imagination, or thought, is nothing except the forms and shapes of such things as he has drawn in with the sight of his mind, still more wonderfully varied, and, so to speak, modified. The things which come forth thence in themselves are inanimate, but they become animate from the influx of life from the Lord.

Such persons may still be in no enlightenment, although they are in the imaginative and perceptive faculty. This faculty is twofold; one which comes from the light of Heaven; the other, which comes from fatuous lumen. In the external form both appear alike; but in the internal they are completely different...

The objects of the world... enter through the eye, and store themselves up in the memory, and this evidently under a shape like the visual one; for the things which are reproduced thence are seen inwardly. Hence the imagination of man; the ideas of which are called by the philosophers material ideas. When these objects appear still more interiorly, they present thought.
When sensuous things are subject to the Rational, then sensuous things, from which is the first imagination of man, are enlightened by the light which comes through Heaven from the Lord...
For the thought, which is above the imagination, requires for its objects things which are abstracted from material things.
The Angels have a speech from intellectual ideas... but Spirits have a speech from the ideas of the imagination, which are called material ideas...
The things there are for the most part imaginary things and fallacies.

The Spirits and Angels who are from the Earth Jupiter, relate in the Grand Man to the imaginative of thought, and thus to an active state of the interior parts: but the Spirits of our Earth relate to the various functions of the exterior parts of the body, into which, when they Want to exercise dominion, the imaginative of thought cannot inflow.
As the Spirits of... Jupiter relate in the to the imaginative of thought, they speak little, and think much...
Sensuous good... is that which is called the pleasure and delight which affects the imaginative thought, which thought is from such things as are merely earthly, corporeal, and worldly...
Man's exteriors which are in the natural world are all things which are of his... external memory, and which are thence of thought and imagination...
That to the natural man, regarded in himself, belongs the material imagination... References.
But that the genuine Cogitative and imaginative is from the internal... man, when the natural man sees, acts, and lives from it. References.
But thought separated from common perception falls into the imagination, [which comes] from sight and from proprium.
What is dignity... in itself but a kind of imaginary thing?
All who are in Hell are nothing but concupiscences of evil and the derivative imaginations of falsity...
All the imaginations of falsity are from Own intelligence.
That it was then disclosed that their reasonings... about faith alone were imaginary and visionary. Signified.
The heads = the imaginary and visionary things with them concerning faith alone.
That their argumentations for faith alone are imaginary and visionary...
Faith without charity is an imaginative...
Then the Lord dispersed those imaginary Heavens.
Many will believe that (these things) are inventions of the imagination.
Every man who has longed for Heaven... is after death introduced into the joys of his imagination.
Those are in the phantasies of their concupiscences who think interiorly in themselves, and indulge their imagination too much...
From this he concludes many things which are nevertheless imaginary.
As (infants) learn to prattle... there arises something obscure, of phantasy; and as this grows clearer, there is born what is obscure of imagination; and thence, of thought.
This is imaginative, and thence is of the lungs.
That this faith... is not possible, and therefore is imaginary.
To this lower mind, which man has in common with brute animals, is attributed imagination; and its ideas are called material ones; while the operation of the intellectual mind is called thought.
The exercitations themselves or what are excited into act, are that which is called imagination.

From this is born a second substance, which is that in which these changes are carried on which are thoughts: and from this again a third substance, in which come forth the changes of state which are called imagination: this is the memory itself.
The activity (of Spirits), which forms a sphere, answers to every thought and imagination of man, and thus acts.
(On various kinds of imaginations; that is, representations.)

There are also imaginations of the more interior and of the inmost Heaven; but as this imagination is not like the Sensitive of sight, but like the Sensitive of the understanding; therefore, for the sake of distinction, the word imagination may serve for interior things; speculation for more interior things; and thought for inmost things.

Does not understand whence come the ideas of imagination, which in like manner consist of myriads of more interior things... (For) an imaginative idea is not in itself an intellectual one, but comes forth such from intellectual ones.
With some the thoughts are exactly as in man, together with his speculation and imagination... The whole of this composite idea, or imaginative representation, is wont to be communicated to Spirits.

Then the Spirits keep his mind, and thus his imagination, in the representation of some thing... and so long as his imagination is kept in things of this kind, he is persuaded that he sees such things... SE 1753.
To whatever sound Spirits... direct their hearing, together with their imagination... the speech is heard in like manner...
a. So that Spirits could see the several objects in the world; and those in the imagination; and those in the thought.
For the possessions of goods in the world is nothing but what is imaginative; and when the imagination possesses them to the full and in its eye, it then possesses them as in the world...
Their phantasies are turned into pleasant shapes of representations, which are imaginative... These representations are such phantasies as are turned into beautiful imaginative ideas...

Such so-called imaginations are real, because they have real things in them: and therefore it was then given to say... that I am willing... to bestow on others all the gold and silver I possess in the world, if I am allowed to possess such imaginative wealth, only retaining (the necessaries of life).
The region of the heel consists of those who enjoy the like imaginations...

So, there remain and return passim in the other life the imaginations taken up from sight; as beautiful lawns, gardens, palaces, and the like, with which they had been delighted in their life. Souls are introduced into the like after death... until they come into better ones.
Thither their imagination and interior man leads them; namely, to the ultimate of order, which is the body.
I spoke with Spirits about pertinacity, that it is of imagination...
What phantasies are, and what imaginations.
We afterwards spoke about angelic representations, that they are not, although they appear... Such things are imaginations, or imaginative representations... Therefore they are not phantasies...
For the memory of particular things contains visual images, which are of the imagination.
From which memory is speculation, which is as it were... the imagination of things: of its imagination is thought, which is their speech.
When I was writing in imagination...
As the imaginative force which (Polhem) had in the body, still remains...
By means of imagination and phantasy (all others) can present the like...
This memory is imaginative, formed from the visible things in the world...
I have sometimes been in a certain light, in which the imagination was as it were withdrawn in a lively manner...
As the natural man... has not any understanding; but only thought from the memory, which is a species of imagination from the objects of sight and hearing...
An inundating rain, and a wind of storms = false and imaginary things rushing in in abundance, which cause that nothing of truth can be seen, and thus destroy the man. AE 644:26.
The Church which... seizes imaginary things for spiritual truths. Signified.
The imaginary things which are from the fallacies of the senses are signified by the horses of Egypt on which they lean.
The horses of Egypt = imaginary things which in themselves are dead, because they are fallacies.
By imaginary things which are from fallacies... Signified.
The horses of Pharaoh = imaginary things, because fallacies, which are scientifics from a perverted Intellectual applied to confirm falsities.
Horses = falsities which are imaginary things.
Man can... easily be carried into falsities completely opposite to truths, by means of continual conclusions from an adopted principle of imagination, that is, an imaginary one.
This perception... is phantasy or imagination.
